results.title: Achievements of ‘New Economy’ must be measured by sustained improvements in economic growth, employment and productivity – Dr. Nsafoah
results.content: In his commentary on the budget titled “Ghana's 2027 Budget: From Macroeconomic Stability to Prioritising Public Investment”, Dr. Nsafoah said the 2027 Budget identifies a markedly larger public investment envelope, communicates a mainly domestic financing strategy and offers a measured formal reserve-adequacy benchmark. “These are reasons for a constructive assessment, not a guarantee of success”.

results.title: Methane cuts offer cheap, fast route to tackling global warming – UN climate chief
results.content: UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell has urged governments to accelerate efforts to reduce methane and other super pollutants, describing them as one of the fastest, cheapest and most effective ways to slow global heating in the near term. He says tackling these emissions could also generate significant economic gains, improve public health and strengthen agricultural production.

results.title: NACOC arrests man who allegedly swallowed 58 cocaine pellets before India trip
results.content: The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has arrested a 58-year-old man at the Accra International Airport after he was reportedly found to have swallowed 58 pellets suspected to contain cocaine. The suspect was preparing to travel to India when he was identified during the Commission’s routine passenger pre-screening operations. According to NACOC, subsequent examination revealed that he had ingested the pellets in an apparent attempt to conceal the suspected narcotic substance and transport it across international borders.

results.title: Asiedu Nketia credits NDC’s 2024 victory to nationwide branch reorganisation
results.content: Outgoing National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketia, says the party’s decision to reorganise its branches nationwide was a key part of the strategy that helped secure its victory in the 2024 general election. In an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse, Mr Asiedu Nketia said the party moved away from its usual approach after the election and focused on addressing organisational weaknesses at the grassroots level. “We went back to branches and made sure that we did proper branch reorganisation. And to address the challenges that we had there,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketia said the party identified regions where it had struggled electorally and sought to understand the reasons for its performance.

results.title: ‘I don’t wait to be chased out’ – Asiedu Nketia on leaving NDC chairmanship
results.content: Outgoing National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketia, says he kept his decision not to seek re-election secret, including from his closest friends, until the final stages of the party’s nomination process. In an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse, Mr Asiedu Nketiah said he deliberately avoided discussing his plans with others because he feared appeals from friends and party members could pressure him into reconsidering. He said his decision reflected a personal belief that leaders should leave positions on their own terms rather than wait to be forced out. “I don't wait to be chased out. I always leave when I'm still living. People may say, ‘Oh, he should have stayed longer.’ But life is made up of choices, and I've made my choice,” he said.

results.title: Ghana’s GH¢28.8 Billion Bond Buyback: A step towards restoring financial confidence
results.content: Government’s planned buyback of GH¢28.8 billion in domestic bonds is an important development in Ghana’s continuing effort to restore confidence in its public finances. Although the figures may appear technical, the underlying issue is quite simple. Government is preparing to settle a substantial debt obligation before it becomes due in February 2027. It is a move that deserves attention, not merely because of the amount involved, but because of what it says about the management of public money.
